ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point $D$ is on side $AB$, $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$, $CF \parallel AB$, and $CF$ intersects the extension line of $DE$ at point $F$. If $AB=4$ and $CF=3$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $CF\parallel AB$, \\
thus $\angle A=\angle ACF$, $\angle F=\angle ADE$, \\
since E is the midpoint of side $AC$, \\
then $AE=CE$, \\
in $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CFE$, \\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle A=\angle ACF \\
\angle ADE=\angle F \\
AE=CE
\end{array}\right.$, \\
therefore $\triangle ADE\cong \triangle CFE$ (AAS), \\
thus $AD=CF=3$, \\
hence $BD=AB-AD=4-3=\boxed{1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; D is located on side AB; E is located on side AC, and line segment DE continues to extend rightward to point F; a line segment is drawn from C to F, and this line segment is parallel to the direction of AB but opposite in direction. Reasoning: According to the vector method, let A be the origin, let B correspond to vector b, and |b|=AB=4, and let C correspond to vector c. Because D is on AB, D=λb can be written. Because CF is parallel to AB, and in the figure the direction of CF is opposite to the direction from A to B, CF=3, so F=c−μb, where μ=CF/AB=3/4. E is the midpoint of AC, so E=c/2. Also because D, E, F are collinear, and E is between D and F, let E=(1−t)D+tF. Substituting gives c/2=(1−t)λb+t(c−μb)=tc+[(1−t)λ−tμ]b. Comparing the coefficients of c gives t=1/2; then comparing the coefficients of b gives (1/2)λ−(1/2)μ=0, so λ=μ=3/4. Therefore AD=λ·AB=(3/4)·4=3, BD=AB−AD=4−3=1.
